blocks: Figure 12: This graph isolates pro- and anti-gun bill proposals in the six months prior and the two years
following the shooting at Sandy Hook. Two key points are highlighted: the shooting, which occurred in
December 2012, and the failure of the Manchin-Toomey bill, which sought to extend background checks to
all gun sales. The defeat of the Manchin bill was largely seen as an NRA victory.
Figure 11: This graph displays pro- and anti-gun bill proposals from 2010 through the end of 2018. There is a
major spike that occurs in January 2013, which was the month directly after the Sandy Hook shooting where 20
first graders and 6 teachers were murdered. This shooting returned gun control to the legislative agenda, and
average bill proposal levels began to increase throughout the years following Sandy Hook.
